question.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: $$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]. $$ The complementary solution to this system is given by $$ {x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R. $$ Then, the general solution of the system is
$x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+$ {{field-1}} $\cdot \,\,$ $-1$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also exponential, i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}],
$$

where $a,b$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=-3{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ -3[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-3a \\ -3b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2b \\ 2a\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-3a \\ -3b\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2b+1 \\ 2a+5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2b+1=-3a \\ 2a+5=-3b\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get 

$$
-2b+1=-3a\,⇒\,a=\frac{2b-1}{3}.
$$

 
Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $b,$ we have

$$
2(\frac{2b-1}{3})+5=-3b\,⇒\,4b-2+15=-9b\,⇒\,b=-1.
$$

So,

$$
a=\frac{2(-1)-1}{3}=\frac{-2-1}{3}=-1.
$$

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)={e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
